account.note: PULLED LIVE AT 11:22 ET AGAINST THE MANDATED ACCOUNT, not carried forward from the 10:22 read even though every figure is identical - identical because nothing has traded, which is a conclusion from a fresh pull rather than an assumption that let the pull be skipped. Portfolio, equity positions and option positions were each queried live and all three returned first time: 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits and ZERO unsettled, with buying_power reading 1009.16 to match. The entire balance is settled, so the whole of it is deployable and no good-faith violation is reachable. ZERO equity orders exist on a created_at floor of 2026-08-22, which is what established that the 09:46 BJ specification had never been executed and was therefore still killable - and IT WAS KILLED THIS HOUR, so the 389.40 it would have deployed is released and the full 1009.16 is uncommitted with no live specification standing against it for the first time today.

entryWatch.setup: BJ post-earnings day-2 continuation off the 8/21 beat - SPECIFIED at 09:46 at a 97.35 limit for 4 shares and WITHDRAWN at 11:22 when the name left the level behind
entryWatch.trigger: KILLED AT 11:22 ON A PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATION, BY APPENDING, AND THE LIMIT WAS NOT RAISED. BJ is 99.62 bid / 99.90 ask at 15:22:37.750553749Z, last 99.720, +3.32% against the 96.42 close, on a 0.281% spread. The 09:46 entry wrote three invalidations and the THIRD has triggered: a bid above 99.00 at any hourly re-quote means the 97.35 limit has stopped being a pullback entry and has become a level the name left behind. The bid is 0.62 above that line. The other two are untouched - the lowest five-minute close today is still 97.130, so nothing has closed below either the 96.42 day-1 close or the 96.895 session low. The crossing is dated from bars rather than asserted: the 10:30 bar closed at exactly 99.000, the 10:35 bar closed 99.270 as the first close through it, and every bar since has closed above, to a 100.090 session high in the 11:00 bar. So it crossed between the 10:22 re-quote and this one and no hour passed with the invalidation unacted. THE HARDER FINDING: the limit was MARKETABLE two minutes after publication. Fifteen-second bars show roughly 1,600 shares printing at or below 97.35 between 09:48:00 and 09:51:45 - 97.300, 97.120, 97.130, 97.245, 97.330, 97.290, 97.204 - against an order for four shares. It was available and it went untaken, which is the second consecutive specification of which that is true. That is evidence about the human gate, NOT a licence to re-strike: no replacement BJ level is written at 99.62 or any other price.
entryWatch.why: THE KILL IS THE ENTRY'S OWN INSTRUCTION BEING HONOURED BY A RUN THAT DID NOT WRITE IT, which is the whole reason the 09:46 entry wrote its invalidations down in advance. It named 99.00 outcome-blind, five hours before the tape reached it, precisely so that an hourly run which had not seen the morning could test it mechanically rather than substitute a fresher opinion. The bid is 99.62 and the level is dead. What this row is really recording is the tension that makes it worth reading: the thesis was RIGHT - a day-2 continuation off a 14.3% beat, bought on the fade, in a name green against a red tape - and BJ has extended 3.32% while QQQ fell 1.14%, exactly as the entry argued it would. The fill was available at the specified price for close to four minutes after publication, on roughly 1,600 shares of depth against a four-share order. And the position does not exist, because the specification requires a human and the human did not act. So the correct response is to kill the level and file the miss against the gate, not to chase the name to 99.62 - re-striking a dead level higher is the behaviour this board has refused most often, it is the third constraint attached to the 2026-08-18 loosening, and a board that honours it only when it is cheap does not honour it at all. FUTU was left dead on 8/21 at the maximum of temptation and BJ is left dead today at the maximum of vindication, which are the two hard cases and this board has now taken both.

entryWatch.setup: FUTU - the 117.90 limit this board published on 8/21 and WITHDREW at 11:21 the same day, now back within half a dollar of the level it was killed at
entryWatch.trigger: DEAD, LEFT DEAD, AND NOW 1.76 BELOW THE WITHDRAWN LEVEL RATHER THAN 0.06 BELOW IT. FUTU is 116.14 bid / 116.28 ask at 15:22:51.451624464Z, last 116.280, down 6.07% from a 123.64 close. The 117.90 limit this board withdrew on 8/21 has now been through three consecutive re-quotes today - 0.49 ABOVE it at 09:46, 0.06 BELOW it at 10:22, and 1.76 BELOW it now. The dead level keeps getting cheaper and it stays dead. A level this board withdrew in writing does not become live again because the tape came back under it, and the 8/21 15:22 finding that the drought test which killed it was pointed at the wrong window is a reason to repair the TEST, not a licence to re-enter the trade. Not re-struck, not entered, and re-verified on a live quote this hour rather than left standing on a stale one.
entryWatch.why: LEFT DEAD DELIBERATELY, AT THE MAXIMUM OF TEMPTATION, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ROW. A level this board killed in writing does not become live again because the tape wandered back to it. The 15:22 run on 8/21 established that the drought test which killed this specification was pointed at the wrong window - 9,381 shares traded below the 117.90 limit in the three and a half minutes after it went live, and the test began measuring 45 seconds after the last sub-limit print. That finding is a reason to repair the TEST, not a licence to buy the trade back. If the board exempted the one name it could prove it had killed wrongly, the 2026-08-18 rule against re-striking a dead level would be worth nothing the first morning it cost something. Today's entry buys a name this board merely DECLINED and refuses a name this board KILLED, and that distinction is the whole of the rule.

entryWatch.setup: BEKE post-earnings day-2 - the largest beat on the board and the candidate today's entry came closest to taking
entryWatch.trigger: DECLINED ON ITS TAPE, NOT ON ITS NUMBER - AND THE TAPE HAS CORROBORATED THE REFUSAL A FOURTH TIME. Q2 0.42 against 0.28, a 50% beat, larger than BJ's 14.3%, on a spread far tighter than BJ's. What refuses it: Friday it gapped to 17.935 and sold all the way to 16.960, THROUGH the prior close, before closing 17.75; today it opened 18.055, printed 18.47 inside five minutes and gave every cent back. Re-quoted this hour at 17.83 bid / 17.84 ask at 15:22:54.314941838Z, up 0.45% against a 17.75 close and 0.19 BELOW the 18.02 it was declined at - a fourth consecutive failure to hold a pop, and lower again than the 17.88 of an hour ago. A 50% beat that cannot hold an opening pop on three consecutive sessions is a beat the market has already priced. Becomes interesting again only on a five-minute close back above 18.47 on volume.
entryWatch.why: THE STRONGEST NUMBER ON THE BOARD ATTACHED TO THE WEAKEST TAPE, which is why it is on the watch list rather than in the order. A 50% beat is more than three times BJ's, the spread is a quarter of BJ's, and the size fits. Every static measure favours BEKE. What refuses it is behaviour rather than measurement: a name that gaps up and sells through its prior close on the print day, then gaps up and gives back a 0.45 pop within fifteen minutes the next session, is telling you who is using the strength. The 2026-08-10 tiebreak says that when a quoted number and a written thesis disagree, the number decides - and here the numbers disagree with each other, the beat against the tape. The tape is the one measured after the beat was known, so it is the one carrying the newer information.

entryWatch.setup: UI post-earnings - the biggest beat of the cohort and the cleanest item 5 failure available
entryWatch.trigger: REFUSED BY A MECHANICAL LIMIT BEFORE ANY VIEW REACHES IT: one share at 534.13 bid is 52.9% of a 1009.16 account against the 40% single-name ceiling, so no quantity of UI is buyable here. The tape says the same thing independently - it beat by 19.4%, 4.73 against 3.96, then opened 8/21 at 597.00 which was the HIGH OF THE DAY, sold to 515.00, closed 559.00, and is down another 4.4% today. A 19% beat that opens at its high and loses 13.7% intraday is the textbook crowded-bulls unwind item 5 describes.
entryWatch.why: A MECHANICAL REFUSAL AND A THESIS REFUSAL POINTING THE SAME WAY, recorded because they are independent and either alone would be enough. The ceiling is arithmetic and needs no judgement: 534.13 against 1009.16 is 52.9%, so there is no quantity of UI that fits under 40%, and the question of whether UI is a good trade is never reached. Had it been reached, item 5 answers it - this is the cleanest crowded-bulls unwind on the board, a 19.4% beat that opened AT the high of the day and lost 13.7% intraday before losing another 4.4% today. Kept on the list as the counter-example that makes today's entry legible: the biggest beat of the cohort produced the worst tape, which is exactly what item 5 predicts and exactly why the size of a beat is not the ranking.

entryWatch.setup: WMT post-earnings day-3 - the best liquidity on the board, declined on arithmetic
entryWatch.trigger: NOT A DISLIKE, AN ARITHMETIC REFUSAL. WMT beat 0.81 against 0.74 on 8/20, is up 1.63% at a 105.38 bid into a red tape, and quotes a 0.019% spread - the tightest on this list by an order of magnitude. What kills it is the exit framework: a +20% target off 105.38 is 126.46 inside five sessions, which is not a move this name produces, so target, stop and time stop would all be decoration rather than levels. Kept on watch because the relative strength is real and would matter to a rulebook with a smaller profit target.
entryWatch.why: THE RULEBOOK REFUSING A GOOD SETUP ON ITS OWN ARITHMETIC, which is worth logging rather than quietly passing over. Everything about WMT is right except the exit framework: real beat, day 3, best liquidity on the board by an order of magnitude, green into a red tape. But take-profit is fixed at +20% and the time stop at about five sessions, and 126.46 by 8/28 is not a number this name produces. An entry whose target cannot realistically be hit is an entry whose exits are decoration, and the 2026-08-10 note is explicit that the 10%-a-day objective may not waive a checklist item or lengthen a time stop to make a trade work. So the refusal is recorded as what it is - a constraint of this rulebook meeting a name it is not built for, not a judgement that WMT is a bad hold.

entryWatch.setup: PDD - reported this morning before the open, day 1
entryWatch.trigger: THE SPIKE DAY ITEM 2 EXISTS TO REFUSE, judged on the least informative fifteen minutes of tape in the week. Q2 2.85 actual against 2.77, a 2.9% beat - the smallest of the cohort - and the stock is 88.61 bid at 13:42:27Z, up just 0.26% from an 88.38 close. Its options were pulled as the alternative instrument and are the worst quoted today: the 9/18 88 call is 3.60 / 6.10 on a 4.85 mark, a 51.5% spread with ZERO open interest. Re-examine on 8/25 as a day-2 candidate if the reaction holds.
entryWatch.why: DAY 1 IS THE ONE DAY ITEM 2 NAMES OUTRIGHT, and the beat is the smallest of the cohort at 2.9%, so there is no tension to resolve here. The row exists mostly to carry the option evidence: PDD was the best remaining candidate for an actual options entry - deep liquid chain, three expirations inside the 3-6 week window, and no earnings inside any of them now that it has reported - and its quotes are the worst on the board. Two ATM strikes with ZERO open interest and spreads over 47%, and the only contract with real depth still at 26.9%. That is the strongest available refutation of the idea that the option finding was ever about the account being small.

entryWatch.setup: The AI, semiconductor and nuclear complex into NVDA on 8/26 and MRVL on 8/27
entryWatch.trigger: REFUSED BY THE moves.json BRANCH WRITTEN SIX SESSIONS IN ADVANCE, and today is the session that branch was written for. The complex is being sold hard - SMCI down 5.8% at 35.09, IONQ down 5.3% at 42.48, OKLO down 5.2% at 39.85, SMR down 5.2% at 8.90, SOUN down 3.2%, ADI down 1.4%, KEYS down 2.5% - and a name that is down 5% into an event is exactly what a sympathy entry looks like when it is rationalised as a discount. The branch refuses entries in this complex on 8/25, 8/26 and 8/27 into either print, and the arithmetic behind it is unchanged: a -8% stop does not survive an event whose implied move is wider than 8%. AMD remains separately refused on the single-name ceiling.
entryWatch.why: WRITTEN SIX SESSIONS BEFORE IT BOUND AND BINDING NOW, which is the test of whether writing branches in advance does anything. The arithmetic has not changed: a -8% stop does not survive an event whose implied move is wider than 8%, so the realistic bad case gaps through the exit rather than filling at it - the same reasoning that refused SMCI at a 14.4% implied move. What today adds is the correlation evidence in live form. OKLO is down 5.32% and SMR is down 5.32%, identical to the second decimal, and IONQ and SMCI are within half a point of both. Four names off this list is not four positions; it is one position at four times the size, paying four spreads, with a stop all four gap through together. Today's entry is deliberately outside this complex, and BJ being held across both prints is a decision stated in the specification rather than an oversight.

entryWatch.setup: KLAR - bouncing off 14.00 after collapsing on its own 8/18 beat
entryWatch.trigger: A FALLING KNIFE RATHER THAN A SETUP THIS BOOK BUYS. KLAR beat on 8/18, 0.01 against a -0.06 estimate, and the stock fell 22.8% that session - 19.51 close to 15.06 - on 34.5 million shares against a 3 million run rate, then kept going to 14.00 by 8/20. It is 14.51 bid today, up 1.3%. Whatever the market objected to in that report is not visible in the EPS line, and buying the third bounce off the low of a 26% four-session decline is averaging into a name the tape has already judged. Not a candidate at any price until it makes a higher low.
entryWatch.why: THE SETUP THAT LOOKS MOST LIKE THIS BOOK'S FAVOURITE AND IS ACTUALLY ITS OPPOSITE. A recent beat and a bounce off a round number reads as a post-earnings pullback entry, and it is not one: the pullback this rulebook buys is a day-2/3 pause after strength, whereas KLAR has fallen 26% in four sessions FROM its beat. Whatever the market objected to in that report is not in the EPS line, and 34.5 million shares against a 3 million run rate says the objection was held with conviction. Buying the third bounce off the low is averaging into a name the tape has already judged, which the rulebook lists under 'does not fit' by name. Not a candidate at any price until it makes a higher low.
